summary: A Slack app that works in your own workspace is quick to build. To let other companies install it you add an OAuth flow, and unlisted distribution needs no review. Listing in the Slack Marketplace adds a content review, and Slack now wants 10 active installs before you can submit.

verdict.headline: Minutes to install in your own workspace and no review for unlisted distribution, but the Marketplace needs 10 active workspace installs first and Slack publishes no review time.

effort.label: Half a day to a working install, 1 to 2 more days for Marketplace materials

prerequisites.detail: Required to install in any workspace other than your own. Use a state parameter and verify requests with signing secrets.

prerequisites.item: SSL on your redirect and request URLs, plus an onboarding flow
prerequisites.detail: Direct hands-on support does not scale across many workspaces.

prerequisites.item: A landing page, support page and privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: Needed for Marketplace review. The privacy policy covers collection, use, retention and deletion requests.

steps.title: Create the app and choose scopes
steps.detail: Pick the fewest scopes that deliver your feature. Slack reviews scopes under least privilege and generally rejects legacy or restricted ones.

steps.title: Install it in your own workspace and test
steps.detail: An app that stays in one workspace is installed from the app dashboard and gets one access token.

steps.title: Build the OAuth flow for many workspaces
steps.detail: Issue a token per workspace and user. Send a state parameter, verify incoming requests with signing secrets, store tokens securely, and use TLS 1.2 or higher.

steps.title: Meet the distribution checklist
steps.detail: SSL everywhere, an onboarding flow, and a least-privilege scope list that workspace admins may review.

steps.title: Activate public distribution for pilots
steps.detail: You get an Add to Slack button and an install link. Good for early customers.

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspace installs
steps.detail: Slack requires at least 10 installs on active workspaces before you can submit, and you must keep them through review.

steps.title: Prepare the Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Short description of 10 words or fewer, images in an 8:5 ratio, support and landing pages, a privacy policy, at least one app collaborator. A 30 to 90 second video is recommended, not required.

steps.title: Submit and respond to review
steps.detail: Slack installs and tests your app. Resubmit after substantial changes. Slack may run a security review at any time after submission.

limits.title: 10 active installs before you can submit
limits.detail: Applies from July 2026 and must hold through review. The page read does not say whether test or internal workspaces count.

limits.title: Some workspaces will not let you in
limits.detail: Some block installs or allow only Marketplace apps, and admin approval may be required for unlisted apps.

limits.title: Broad scopes get a closer look
limits.detail: Apps asking for broad data access or admin scopes receive enhanced review.

blockers.problem: You cannot submit: fewer than 10 active installs
blockers.why: The install minimum is a hard gate for Marketplace submission.
blockers.nextMove: Run unlisted pilots with the install link until you reach 10 active workspaces.

blockers.problem: A customer's workspace blocks your app
blockers.why: Some workspaces allow only Marketplace apps or require admin approval.
blockers.nextMove: Give the customer's admin a short scope explanation, or plan the Marketplace listing for that segment.

blockers.problem: A scope is rejected in review
blockers.why: Each scope needs a justification tied to functionality Slack can test.
blockers.nextMove: Drop the scope, or show exactly where the feature uses it.

blockers.problem: You cannot plan around the review
blockers.why: The page read gives no review turnaround, only a 2 business day reply time for support requests.
blockers.nextMove: Plan launch dates with slack time and keep running unlisted pilots while you wait.

agentCanDo: Map your features to least-privilege Slack scopes and draft the justification for each
Write the OAuth install handler, request-signature check and token storage code for you to review
Draft the landing page, support page, privacy policy and listing copy
Track your active install count and tell you when you reach 10
Create the Composio auth config once you have a client ID and secret
youMustDo: Create the app in your Slack account and install it in your workspace
Activate public distribution and share the install link with pilot customers
Provide listing images and a video if you make one
Submit to the Marketplace and answer reviewer questions

uncertainties: Slack publishes no review turnaround on the pages read. Only the 2 business day support reply time is stated.
The distribution guide page read does not mention the 10-install minimum; it appears in a September 2026 changelog, so other docs pages may lag behind it.
The changelog post is dated 2026-09-01, but says the rule applies as of July 2026 with no exact day. It does not define an 'active workspace' or name the earlier threshold.
Whether test, internal or your own workspaces count toward the 10 installs is not stated.
